strategy.summary: Add a small, read-only Playwright smoke suite (tests/shop.smoke.spec.js, every test titled with @smoke) for the Kettle & Co. tea shop that checks a deployed build's critical paths through the configured baseURL (BASE_URL, or the locally started shop): the health endpoint answers, the catalogue lists the products, a product page opens from it, adding to the cart (a browser cookie only, no server request) shows in the cart, and the checkout form is reachable. No test submits an order or sends POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE.
inScope: Catalogue page (/) heading and product links
Product page reached from the catalogue: heading, price, Add to cart button
Add to cart (client-side cookie) reflected on the cart page: line, quantity, total, header count
Checkout page with a cart: order form fields and Place order button visible (not submitted)
A test:smoke npm script that runs only @smoke tests
outOfScope: Placing an order (POST /orders) and the order confirmation page: it writes data on the server, so it is left to the full e2e suite (tests/checkout.spec.js)
Error paths (404 page, empty-cart checkout refusal, 405) — smoke covers critical paths only
Running the tests in this run: the target is a deployed, non-disposable build; the PR's CI runs them
assumptions: The product catalogue (PRODUCTS in src/catalogue.js) ships with the build, so every deployed environment shows the same products; tests import PRODUCTS and formatPrice from src/catalogue.js rather than copying values.
Adding to the cart writes only the browser's cart cookie (public/app.js) and makes no server request, so it is read-only for the deployment and allowed in smoke.
The app has no access control (no login), so no credentials are needed.
Every first-party service runs for real: locally Playwright's existing webServer starts the shop; with BASE_URL set, the tests hit the deployed build. Nothing is faked.

risks.description: A deploy that serves pages but whose client script (/app.js) is broken makes the cart unusable while pages still load
risks.mitigation: TC4 clicks Add to cart and checks the cart page shows the line, which needs /app.js to run

risks.description: Smoke tests accidentally write data in production
risks.mitigation: No test submits the checkout form or sends a non-GET request; checkout test only asserts the form is shown

acceptanceCriteria.text: The deployed app is up: GET /health answers 200 with {"status":"ok"}
The catalogue home page loads and lists every product the shop sells, each linking to its product page
A user can open a product page from the catalogue and see its name, price and an Add to cart button
A user can add a product to the cart and see it in the cart with its quantity and total
A user with items in the cart can reach the checkout page and see the order form
Every smoke test is tagged @smoke in its title, only reads (no data created, changed or deleted on the server), and reaches the app only through the configured baseURL
acceptanceCriteria.metBy: All tests live in tests/shop.smoke.spec.js, carry @smoke in their titles, use relative URLs against Playwright's baseURL (BASE_URL or the local shop), and make only GET requests; a test:smoke script runs `playwright test --grep @smoke`.

testCases.title: health endpoint reports the shop is up @smoke
testCases.rationale: Critical path: the build starts and answers at all.

testCases.title: catalogue lists every product @smoke
steps: Check a link per product in PRODUCTS with exact name and href /products/<id>
testCases.expected: Heading shown and a link for each product to its page
testCases.rationale: Critical path: the shop's front page renders the catalogue users browse.

testCases.title: opens a product page from the catalogue @smoke
testCases.expected: URL is /products/teapot; heading 'Cast-iron teapot', price £48.00 and an Add to cart button are shown
testCases.rationale: Critical path: product pages are where users start buying.

testCases.title: shows a product added to the cart in the cart @smoke
steps: Check status 'Added to your cart' and header link 'Cart (1)'
testCases.expected: Cart page heading 'Your cart', a row with cells 'Cast-iron teapot', '1', '£48.00', and Total £48.00
testCases.rationale: Critical path: the cart works (client script loads and the server reads the cookie) — cookie only, no server write.

testCases.title: shows the order form at checkout @smoke
steps: Open /products/teapot and click Add to cart
testCases.expected: Heading 'Checkout'; Name, Email and Address fields and a 'Place order' button are visible; the form is not submitted
testCases.rationale: Critical path: users can reach the step where they pay, without placing an order.

strategy.environmentNotes: Playwright baseURL is BASE_URL when set (deployed build); otherwise playwright.config.js starts `node src/server.js` on localhost:4175. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs `npx playwright test`, which includes the new file. Tests are not run in this TestForge run.

refusals.reason: tests/shop.smoke.spec.js written before testforge:api, testforge:playwright were loaded
`playwright` runs tests, and this run writes a smoke suite for http://host.docker.internal:57359, which isn't marked disposable, without running it.

candidates.text: In smoke-suite runs against a non-disposable target, run_command refuses any `playwright` command, including `playwright test --list`. Check the specs with run_checks and self_check only. Neither has anything to run here, since the repo has no lint or typecheck scripts.
candidates.evidence: SMOKE-20261120-3155: run_command 'npx playwright test --list' refused; run_checks: 'No repository checks apply to the changed files.'
